title: The Rich Fool
reflectionText: The harvest was good, and every plan the man made was for himself — bigger barns, years of goods laid up, his own soul told to take its ease and eat and drink. Every word of his reasoning was about a future he assumed was his. He was told that night that the future was not. What is it to store so carefully for years you were never promised?
editorialNotes: Text-First Story Factory 2.0 Batch B (Full-Canon Production Gate CG14, approved 2026-07-23). Luke 12:13-21, absent both lanes; adjacent 1011 covers Luke 12:22-31 (the ravens/lilies worry teaching), which this story stays distinct from. SHORT only, shortScripture (WEB 186w / KJV 185w): the ~181-word parable, retold faithfully with the man's soliloquy given as reported speech and only God's climactic address kept direct, honestly falls below the 300-word SHORT floor; shortScripture:true is set (owner-approved) rather than padding. The inheritance dispute (12:13-14) is the opening frame; the warning about covetousness ('a man's life doesn't consist in the abundance of the things he possesses', 12:15) is preserved; God's address ('You foolish one, tonight your soul is required of you') and the closing 'is not rich toward God' (12:20-21) are kept. No motive or emotion given to the rich man beyond his own stated reasoning; no added explanatory moral paragraph beyond the source; no propositions repeated to reach a floor. Boundary held to vv13-21. KJV lane uses KJV diction (Master, divider, Thou fool); WEB uses the modern register.
